answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public registry before it may submit claims, with rewards delayed until independent peers validate them. A grove of linked accounts then cannot multiply influence for free: every identity ties up capital, and coordinated false claims risk slashing the stake. Raising a sybil swarm to the zenith of influence therefore requires more capital than one attacker can cheaply acquire, while the ocean of ordinary agents can still join with modest stakes.
